text.p: Intellect Holdings Ltd said it will raise its takeover offer for Techway Ltd to an effective 43.8 cents a share in a counter-bid to the revised offer by Nova Pacific Capital Ltd of 38 cents.
Intellect said it will now offer one of its shares for every 2-1/2 Techway shares plus five cents a share cash.
Based on Tuesday's closing price of 97 cents for Intellect, the offer values each Techway share at 43.8 cents and Techway's 12.6 million issued shares at A$5.5 million.
Techway shares closed at 39 cents on Monday.

In a separate statement, Techway said its board unanimously recommended that in the absence of a higher offer, shareholders accept the new Intellect offer and intend accepting for their own shareholdings.
Intellect also said it reduced its minimum acceptance conditions to 70 percent of Techway's issued capital from 90 percent.
Last Thursday, Nova said it would raise its on-market takeover offer for Techway to 38 cents a share from 30 cents and said it now holds 18.7 percent of Tecway's issued capital.
Intellect designs and develops electronic payment systems, including smart card readers and cryptographic processors.
It has been in talks with Techway for some months about Techway's WEB Australia division which provides Internet banking systems.
Ross Leighton, executive chairman of Intellect, said his company would prefer to own 100 percent of Techway.

"We could then fully fund and integrate its operations, however in the light of Nova's desire to have an investment in Techway, we have reduced our minimum acceptance condition considerably," he said.

"I believe that only through our strong banking associations can the full potential and value of WEB be realised and we will only proceed to support WEB if we can achieve a significant level of ownership," Leighton said in a statement.

"I believe that Intellect has the preferred network to establish WEB products on an international basis. Techway shareholders can still participate in this exciting future by accepting Intellect's generous terms," Jon Brett, managing director of Techway, said in the same statement.
Leighton said Intellect would welcome Nova as a shareholder.
